lf-timeline.description: An authored sequence of events over time, one lane per actor, that the reader steps through with Previous and Next while a playhead and a step list follow. Use it to explain an order of events, such as a race between jobs, or to compare several runs of the same sequence on one time axis, such as before and after a fix; use `lf-trace` for a recorded browser journey and `lf-motion` for continuous playback.
lf-timeline.instructions: Write one `lf-lane` per actor, in the order the reader should scan them, and in each an `lf-event` per thing that happened to it. `at` is the event's time in milliseconds from the sequence's start; add `end` for an event with duration, such as work in progress, and leave it out for an instant. Times read as elapsed from the start, such as "1 h 30 min"; for a sequence the reader knows by clock time, such as an incident or an afternoon's session, give the clock time of `at="0"` as an ISO date-time in `start`, such as `start="2026-11-25T12:56"`, and the axis, the step list and the position line read as times of day, such as "15:46", on the clock `start` is written in. Previous and Next visit events in start order: events with the same `at` share one step, and a span's end is not a step, so model a moment the reader must stop at, such as a write landing, as its own instant. A lane or run may give a short form of its `label` in `abbr`, such as `abbr="L"` for a lane labelled "Line fork": the step list under the chart shows the short form and previews the label to a reader pointing at it, while the chart and listeners keep the label. Keep each event's `label` to a short clause, since the prose around the widget carries the explanation; the widget lays labels out so that none overlaps a bar, another label or the playhead. Give every event a page-unique `id`: it is the event's comment target.
lf-timeline.example: <lf-timeline id="deploy-order" aria-label="Deploy order"><lf-lane label="Build"><lf-event id="deploy-compile" at="0" end="4000" label="Compile"></lf-event><lf-event id="deploy-artifact" at="4000" label="Artifact ready"></lf-event></lf-lane><lf-lane label="Release"><lf-event id="deploy-rollout" at="4500" end="9000" label="Roll out"></lf-event></lf-lane></lf-timeline>

lf-lane.description: One actor's row in an `lf-timeline`, holding its events.

lf-run.description: One run of a compared sequence in an `lf-timeline`, such as the run before a fix, holding its lanes. Every run in a timeline shares its time axis and its playhead, and a timeline with runs keeps every lane in one.
lf-run.example: <lf-timeline id="retry-order" aria-label="Retry handling before and after the fix"><lf-run label="Before the fix" abbr="Before"><lf-lane label="Client" abbr="C"><lf-event id="retry-before-send" at="0" end="300" label="Send"></lf-event><lf-event id="retry-before-resend" at="1200" end="1500" label="Resend"></lf-event></lf-lane><lf-lane label="Server" abbr="S"><lf-event id="retry-before-apply" at="400" label="Apply"></lf-event><lf-event id="retry-before-reapply" at="1600" label="Apply again"></lf-event></lf-lane></lf-run><lf-run label="After the fix" abbr="After"><lf-lane label="Client" abbr="C"><lf-event id="retry-after-send" at="0" end="300" label="Send"></lf-event><lf-event id="retry-after-resend" at="1200" end="1500" label="Resend"></lf-event></lf-lane><lf-lane label="Server" abbr="S"><lf-event id="retry-after-apply" at="400" label="Apply"></lf-event><lf-event id="retry-after-skip" at="1600" label="Skip the duplicate"></lf-event></lf-lane></lf-run></lf-timeline>

lf-event.description: One event in a timeline lane: an instant at `at`, or a span from `at` to `end`, in milliseconds.
